chunks: From him, from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Miskān, from Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd al-Khāliq, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the time of ẓuhr. He said: “After the sun’s decline by a foot-length or something near that, except on the day of al-Jumuʿah or during travel, for indeed its time then is when the sun declines.”

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: the sun’s decline from the middle of the sky; solar noon passing
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, which affects the beginning time of the prayer here
key_terms.بِقَدَمٍ: by the measure of a foot-length, indicating a short interval after zawāl
key_terms.تَزُولُ الشَّمْسُ: the sun declines from its zenith
key_terms.وَقْتِ الظُّهْرِ: the appointed time of the ẓuhr salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ: the day of Friday, treated here as an exception in timing

ai.seo_question: When does the time of ẓuhr salat (prayer) begin according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states the time for ẓuhr salat (prayer) as being after zawāl by about a foot-length or close to that. It makes an exception for Friday and for travel, in which cases the time begins immediately when the sun declines.
